problem: Repeated sessions can lose recovered architecture, duplicate semantic authorities, reuse decision identifiers, skip protection and migration stages, or confuse a narrow PASS with system readiness.
scope: Canonical governance package and shared agent entrypoint, strengthened with an architecture-integrity constitution: one authority/owner, recovery before redesign, stop-the-line conflicts, an ordered change state machine, three safety gates, monotonic migration, dirty-tree isolation, persistent continuation ledgers and bounded exceptions. No runtime rewrite, schema migration, deployment or certification.
baseline: b46c0438d4927851fcd688a8a8e71468aba6cf18; pre-existing dirty backend/docs/operations work preserved.
reuse: Extend existing doctrine, canonical tree, AIR/ADR ownership, technical-acceptance and release-gate. No second domain contract registry.
impact: Every Codex/Claude entrypoint now requires DISCOVER -> RECOVER -> DECIDE -> PROTECT -> IMPLEMENT -> MIGRATE -> ELIMINATE -> VERIFY -> GOVERN, and requires Behavior, Architecture and Quality gates before completion. Agent entrypoints -> canonical requirements -> bounded cards -> structural gate -> existing technical/release gates remains the enforcement chain; runtime implementations are unchanged.
compatibility: Existing root policy, M3/M2/M1/M0 authority, requirement catalogue and release checks are retained. The constitution tightens agent behavior without changing runtime contracts. Python 3.9+ remains required for governance gates. Review-range mode still requires an external immutable base/head and clean checkout; local static mode reports coverage NOT_ASSERTED.
failure: Missing/malformed authority, unresolved semantic conflict, skipped stage, failed safety gate, drift or stale evidence fails closed. The policy/checker has no runtime state side effects. Rollback consists of reverting only the shared entrypoint constitution and this card/evidence update; preserve unrelated dirty work.
security: No credentials, database access or deployment. Paths confined to repository; no execution of commands stored in cards. Evidence hashes detect drift but do not authenticate authors.
